name: Tshikona (Venda reed-pipe national dance)
lineage: The national dance of the Venda of the Soutpansberg, performed at chiefs' courts for installations, rituals and other important occasions. Men each blow a single-note end-blown pipe from a graded set, the pipes interlocking in hocket into a single repeating melody, while women play the large ngoma, medium murumba and small thungwa drums. John Blacking's 1950s field recordings, held at the University of Washington Ethnomusicology Archives, and the CNRS-CREM archive document it. The flute card stands in for the pipes and the membrane-drum card for the drums.
